subject: Private GPU pool — throughput playtest & scaling recommendation
messages:
From: Martin Lowe <m.lowe@opticloud.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: infra-eng@opticloud.com
Date: 2028-01-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Private pool playtest request — throughput baseline

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for offering to run a brief playtest on our private deployment. We want to validate two things before we commit to a Dedicated/Private order:

1) Sustained throughput for our peak 5-minute window (goal: 1,800 requests / minute for 512-token prompts).
2) P99 tail latency under 2.5s for the same workload and our planned batching settings.

We can supply a replay of production arrivals (attached sample traffic) and have access to an on-prem H100 cluster (8x H100 nodes) that your team can spin against in our VPC. Can you confirm what telemetry and artifacts you need from our side and an approximate timeline for a 24–48 hour run?

Martin
Infra Lead, OptiCloud Media

Subject: Re: Private pool playtest request — throughput baseline

Martin —

We can run a 36-hour playtest (warm start + sustained peak windows + cold restarts). What we need from you:
- SSH access to the bastion / deployment manifests (we only need read-only to the inference pods and the cluster autoscaler config).
- Exact replay file (we can accept the sample snippet but need the full 60m replay for the peak).
- Allowed windows for kernel / node reboots (if we exercise preemption/failure scenarios).

Planned telemetry we will provide: per-GPU request/sec, per-GPU token/sec, batch sizes distribution, queue lengths, p50/p95/p99 latencies, KV cache hit-rate, and network egress/ingress latency histograms. We'll also provide an artifact bundle (csv + small tar of logs) and a sizing recommendation draft.

Timeline: run starts 2028-01-12 08:00 PST, initial results by 2028-01-12 20:00 PST, final artifacts by 2028-01-13 14:00 PST. Does that work?

Thanks —
Olga
Staff Solution Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2028-01-12T20:03:00-08:00
Subject: Playtest artifacts: initial throughput numbers

Folks —

I uploaded the playtest artifacts from OptiCloud run #1 to the shared drive (link below). Key takeaways from the 12-hour sustained window:

- Workload: 512-token average prompts, replayed arrival curve with 5-minute ramp to 1,800 rpm sustained for 10 minutes, repeated 6x during the run.
- HW: 8x H100 nodes, each node running 4 inference processes (quantized model q8_0, Redwood-2 medium).

Measured baseline:
- Cluster aggregate: peak 2,200 requests/min (36.7 rps) for 5-minute windows; average batch size 6.
- Per-GPU (observed avg): 9.5 requests/sec when warm (512-token), 4.2 requests/sec cold after restart (KV cache miss).
- P50/P95/P99: 380ms / 1.1s / 2.6s during sustained windows.
- KV cache hit-rate: 73% after sustained traffic; prefix caching produced a 2.2x effective throughput improvement vs cold.
- Network: median intra-VPC RTT 1.6ms; occasional microbursts to 12ms coinciding with node IO spikes.

I'll drop the CSV and the sample log snippets: playtest_results_2028-01-12.csv and network-latency-samples-jan10.txt.

Notes: the observed p99 2.6s slightly breaches OptiCloud's target (2.5s). The biggest drivers were cold-starts on a rolling upgrade and two nodes that had transient IO stalls — those correlated with the 12ms microbursts.

Vivek
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/driveid_playtest-2028-01

From: Martin Lowe <m.lowe@opticloud.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: infra-eng@opticloud.com
Date: 2028-01-13T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Playtest artifacts: initial throughput numbers

Thanks Vivek — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications before we meet tomorrow:

- You mention per-GPU warm throughput 9.5 req/sec. Can you translate that into a recommended committed GPU count for our steady-state of 1,800 rpm?
- For the cold-start behavior, are we primarily seeing model load times or filesystem IO throttling? Would a small local NVMe cache per node eliminate most of the misses?

We'd like to avoid over-committing on GPUs because our procurement cycle is long. If we can define a small burst pool and autoscaling guardrails that keep p99 under 2.5s, that would be ideal.

Martin

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Martin Lowe <m.lowe@opticloud.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2028-01-14T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Playtest artifacts: initial throughput numbers

Martin —

Quick answers + a draft sizing recommendation (attached PDF):

1) Baseline committed GPUs:
- Observed warm per-GPU throughput: 9.5 req/s -> ~570 req/min per GPU.
- For steady 1,800 req/min we recommend committing 4 GPUs as the baseline (4 * 570 = 2,280 req/min) to cover sustained load with ~26% headroom.

2) Burst capacity and autoscaling:
- Configure an immediate burst pool of 2 GPUs (pre-warmed) to absorb traffic spikes.
- Autoscaler policy: scale-up threshold at queue length > 40 and sustained for 30s; scale-down cooldown 180s to avoid oscillation.

3) Cold-starts / IO:
- The 4.2 req/s cold throughput suggests model load is the dominant factor, with additional latency from remote model fetch. Local NVMe model cache per node would reduce cold penalty significantly — we measure ~1.8x improvement in cold throughput when model artifacts are local. If procurement prevents NVMe, we recommend a rolling pre-warm job that keeps a minimal KV/cache warm on a pool of standby GPUs.

4) SLO tradeoffs:
- With the recommended baseline + 2 GPU burst pool we project p99 ≈ 2.1s under current arrival patterns; with NVMe cache p99 ≈ 1.6s.

Next steps: Hannah, can you greenlight this recommendation for OptiCloud so we can send a formal sizing quote to procurement? If approved we'll create a short runbook for node maintenance that preserves pre-warmed instances during upgrades.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Product Ops — Private Deployments, Redwood Inference

Attachment: sizing-recommendation-draft.pdf

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Martin Lowe <m.lowe@opticloud.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Playtest artifacts: initial throughput numbers — approval to proceed

Martin / team —

Approved to proceed with Kimberly's recommendation. Key commitments from Redwood:
- Baseline: 4 committed GPUs in OptiCloud's private pool.
- Burst: 2 pre-warmed GPUs that will be available during business-critical windows (08:00–20:00 local).
- NVMe cache: recommend OptiCloud enable local NVMe for model artifacts; if not available, Redwood will provide a pre-warm daemon to maintain cache residency on the burst pool.

Deliverables:
1) formal sizing quote and pricing sheet (by 2028-01-17 17:00 PST)
2) maintenance runbook and upgrade policy (by 2028-01-19)
3) one-week follow-up playtest after caching changes are applied to validate p99 improvements

Martin — please confirm acceptance of these commitments and we'll route to your procurement and infra teams.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
